subject: math

objective.text: Solve additive compare word problems with tape diagrams. Find how much more or fewer.

explanations.title: What compare means
explanations.text: To compare, put two amounts side by side. The difference tells how much more or fewer one is.

explanations.title: How much more
explanations.text: Draw two tapes, one for each amount. The unknown is the missing part, the difference. So subtract the smaller from the larger.

explanations.title: Fewer and less
explanations.text: Say fewer when talking about separate things, like apples. Say less for amounts like juice.

explanations.title: Two-step compare
explanations.text: Sometimes you find one amount first. Then draw a new double tape to compare the two amounts.

explanations.title: Three-step compare
explanations.text: Find each amount at first. Use the relationship in the story, like double. Then compare.

A copper wire was 240 meters long. After 60 meters was cut off, how long was it?
The cut copper wire was 180 meters. That is double the steel wire. How long was the steel wire?
At first the copper wire was 240 meters and the steel wire was 90 meters. How much longer was the copper wire?
A mixture of 2 chemicals is 1,034 milliliters. It has 755 milliliters of Chemical B. How many milliliters of Chemical A are in it?
Chemical A is 279 milliliters and Chemical B is 755 milliliters. How much less of Chemical A than Chemical B is in the mixture?
Gavin has 1,094 toy blocks. Avery has 816. How many more blocks does Gavin have?
Container B holds 2,391 liters. Containers A and B together hold 11,875 liters. How many liters does Container A hold?
Container A holds 9,484 liters. Container B holds 2,391 liters. How many more liters does A hold than B?
A yellow yarn was 230 inches long. After 90 inches were cut off, how long was it?
The cut yellow yarn is 140 inches. That is twice the blue yarn. How long is the blue yarn?
At first the yellow yarn was 230 inches and the blue yarn was 70 inches. How much longer was the yellow yarn?

hints.text: Write each unit in its place. Use a zero for any place with none.
Add the parts that are in the right places. Use zero for empty places.
Think how many grams make one kilogram.
Find the whole and the parts you know. Subtract the parts from the whole.
Draw two tapes. Subtract the smaller amount from the larger amount.
Find one amount first. Then compare it with the other amount.
The longer one is double. So the shorter one is half.
Think about which word fits separate things and which fits an amount.

assets_required.why_this_method: The lesson uses tape diagrams drawn by the child. The child cannot draw them here.
assets_required.description: A double tape diagram. Two tapes sit one above the other. The child sets the two amounts, sees the difference as a bracket, and chooses how much more or fewer.
must_show_exactly: Two tapes of different lengths one above the other
A bracket that marks the difference
Labels for the two amounts and a variable for the unknown
A choice of words: more, fewer, less, longer
A single tape with a bracket for a total to start two-step problems
states_or_frames: The difference marked with a bracket
A total tape split into two parts
assets_required.interaction: Child sets the two amounts. The tapes change length and the bracket shows the difference. The child picks add or subtract.
assets_required.alt_text: A double tape diagram with a bracket for the difference.
assets_required.generation_caption: A clean double tape diagram with two labeled bars, a bracket for the difference and a variable. [Build by code]
assets_required.review_notes: Source tape diagrams are drawn by the child. Build from the printed numbers.
